subject: BridgeBank streaming lag: incident timeline, temporary mitigations, and next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@bridgebank.com>, BridgeBank Engineering <eng-team@bridgebank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: BridgeBank streaming lag: preliminary notice

Hi Sam / BridgeBank team —

We’re seeing an elevated rate of latency and chunking delays affecting streaming responses (chat) for BridgeBank sessions in us-west-2. Early telemetry shows a spike in per-request tail latency starting ~09:05 PDT, and some clients are observing pauses between streamed chunks of 3–7s.

What we’re doing now:
- Eng team is running targeted traces on the serving pool for your tenant.
- We’ve queued a short maintenance window to apply an emergency config that reduces per-connection KV cache retention for long conversations.
- Customer-support will keep you updated every 30 minutes until we’ve restored normal streaming cadence.

Short-term customer mitigations you can apply now (minimal client changes):
- If you can tolerate a synchronous response temporarily, switch to non-streaming (full-response) endpoint — this avoids chunk coordination.
- Reduce max_tokens for assistant responses to 512 to reduce KV growth.
- Add client-side retry with exponential backoff (start 250ms) and idempotency tokens if you see stalled streams.

We’ll follow up with a timeline and a postmortem once we’ve stabilized. Apologies for the interruption — we recognize chat is core to your UX and are prioritizing this.

Attachments: streaming-mitigation-checklist.md (checklist of simple client and server flags)

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick questions for your triage team: could this be related to recent long-conversation sessions we migrated last week? Also, what’s the ETA on the emergency config you mentioned?

We’d appreciate ETA and whether there are any steps on our side beyond switching to synchronous responses.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:38:05 -0700
Subject: Re: BridgeBank streaming lag: preliminary notice

Short internal update — I’ve assigned this P1 to Dev and Hannah. Initial triage looks like per-tenant KV cache growth combined with a small subset of sessions that have very long histories (>12k tokens) causing memory pressure on a handful of serving shards. Action plan:

1) Dev: enable per-tenant cache TTL=600s (was 3600s) and purge stale prefixes for BridgeBank shard pool.
2) Hannah: validate autoscaling is bringing the spare workers online and bump spare_count +1 for the pool.
3) Priyom: send the customer the temporary guidance to disable streaming + fallback options (done).

Also preparing the mitigation checklist (attached) with exact client flags and server-side knobs so Support can hand this off to BridgeBank if they want to apply client changes themselves.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@bridgebank.com>, BridgeBank Engineering <eng-team@bridgebank.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 10:02:30 -0700
Subject: Re: BridgeBank streaming lag: preliminary notice

Hi all — preliminary root-cause and mitigations applied:

Root cause (preliminary):
- A small percentage of BridgeBank sessions had very long context windows (12k–18k tokens) after last-week migration. The per-connection KV cache retention caused eviction pressure and increased scheduler queueing on 3 serving shards, producing chunk-delivery delays.

What we applied (10:00 PDT):
- Reduced per-tenant KV cache TTL to 600s for BridgeBank and forced a purge of stale KV entries on affected shards.
- Temporarily enabled autoscale extra_spare=+1 and increased the max-burst capacity for the pool to absorb the load while caches pruning completes.
- Deployed a temporary model-fallback rule: for streaming requests exceeding token_count_threshold=4096, route to a quantized model variant with smaller memory footprint (expected slight quality delta).

Observed effect: streaming cadence returned to normal for ~90% of affected sessions by 10:12 PDT. A small subset of sessions still see 1–2s jitter as caches warm.

Customer-facing mitigations you can adopt immediately (copy/paste friendly):
- Use the non-streaming endpoint for flows where you can tolerate single-response latency; set max_tokens=512.
- Add client-side keepalive and chunk-timeout: if no new chunk within 1.5s, trigger a lightweight HEAD/health probe to the streaming endpoint then retry chunk retrieval with exponential backoff.
- Prefer the prefer_fast_mode flag (if acceptable) to pick a lower-latency runtime variant.

Attachments: 20270522-incident-timeline.pdf (preliminary timeline), streaming-mitigation-checklist.md

We’ll follow up with a full postmortem after logs and traces are correlated.

— Dev
Lead SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@bridgebank.com>, BridgeBank Engineering <eng-team@bridgebank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:42:05 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: incident resolved, next steps and postmortem invite

Hi Sam / BridgeBank team —

Thanks again for the rapid confirmation and patience earlier. Summary and next steps:

- Timeline: issue began ~09:05 PDT; mitigations started at 10:00 PDT; bulk of traffic returned to normal by 10:12 PDT; residual jitter cleared by 12:03 PDT after background cache rebuilds. (See attached timeline PDF)
- Impact: short-term elevated streaming latency and chunk pauses for ~6% of active sessions during the spike. No message loss we’ve observed; most sessions recovered once cache TTL/purge and autoscaling took effect.
- Root cause (prelim): per-tenant KV cache retention + long-history sessions caused eviction and scheduler queueing on a small set of shards. We’ll include a permanent fix in the postmortem.

Customer recommendations for durable resilience (we can help implement these):
1) Apply client-side short-term timeout + retry for streaming chunk reads and consider a synchronous fallback path.
2) Limit conversational window length on critical paths (archive older turns) or use prefix compression.
3) Enable prefer_fast_mode for mission-critical routes where slight quality tradeoff is acceptable.

We’d like to schedule a postmortem review with your engineering team next week (30–45 minutes). Proposed slots: Tue 2027-05-25 09:00 PDT or Wed 2027-05-26 10:00 PDT. Please let me know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite with the postmortem doc.

Attachments: 20270522-incident-timeline.pdf, streaming-mitigation-checklist.md

— Priyom
Priyom Das
